title: Slow-Wave Generation explains slow_wave_density alteration
summary: slow-wave generation may drive measurable change in slow_wave_density among sleep-disorder populations, detectable with EEG features.
content: This hypothesis proposes that slow-wave generation is not merely correlated with sleep disturbance but acts as an organizing mechanism that changes slow_wave_density. The proposal is grounded in 4 evidence records spanning EEG, EEG-fMRI, fMRI. It should be tested by modeling slow_wave_density against mechanism-linked features while controlling for known sleep severity and data-quality covariates.
rationale: The selected evidence contains 4 supportive and 0 uncertain/refuting records. The generation strategy used synthesizing the strongest available evidence into one mechanistic proposal. This keeps the hypothesis anchored to observed variables rather than inventing unavailable measurements.
experimental_plan: Use the analysis-ready profile to identify approved features for slow_wave_density, thalamus_DMN_FC, DMN_FC. Fit a prespecified model with negative controls, then test whether slow-wave generation improves prediction or mediation of sleep outcomes beyond baseline covariates.
novelty_assessment: The novelty comes from connecting slow-wave generation to slow_wave_density through an explicit, testable multimodal bridge rather than treating them as isolated findings.
key_assumptions: slow-wave generation is measurable through available sleep-science features
slow_wave_density captures a downstream expression of the mechanism
The association remains after quality-control and confound checks
